text:
4 more bios/letters/autobios -- shorter books (~100 pgs)

1. Diving Bell and Butterfly - still cannot believe this is a real book. has to be one of the greatest feats in human history

2. Oscar Wilde's "De Profundis" - vicious self-indictment, hall of fame writer just bleeding on the page...probably some of the best writing ever produced on humility, sorrow, suffering, and despair. 

3. Emerson - Self-Reliance and Other Essays. Read all these, arguably required reading...gifted writer, vocabulary, rhythm, no one puts as much power into each sentence. If you finish and want more, buy The Portable Emerson

4. Tolstoy - A Confession. Autobiographical/memoir, spiritual transformation, searching for the meaning of life in the writing of wise men and sages...Solomon, Schopenhauer, Buddha...goes on to find it where all men find it. If ur mind is already there, its aces

4 random bio recs:

1. Roberts' Napoleon bio - required reading for any young philosopher-king with dreams of marching a 600,000-man Grande Armée across the Niemen River

2. River of Doubt - Morris' "Rise of Roosevelt" is required bio reading, but River of Doubt is an easy read - sort of a semi-bio, just an absolutely insane story, well-written. TR is prob #1 pick for American role model

3. Stephen King - On Writing. Never read any of his books - not required. Great writer, great book, half memoir, half writing masterclass. 

4. Prideaux - Nietzsche bio. Is this a GOAT bio, no, but its a grade-A bio on a lunatic of a human. Read this before u read anything he wrote - adds valuable context
